svg.title: Three roads after chemoradiotherapy: trimodality, definitive CRT with salvage, active surveillance
svg.desc: Schematic timeline of three roads after chemoradiotherapy. Road 1, trimodality (CROSS, the Netherlands, n=366, 75% adenocarcinoma, 23% SCC): 5 weeks of chemoradiotherapy (41.4 Gy in 23 fractions plus weekly carboplatin/paclitaxel ×5) → surgery 6–8 weeks after (in-hospital mortality 4% in both arms, R0 92% vs 69%) → pathology pCR 29% (SCC 49%, adenocarcinoma 23%) → median follow-up 147 months: 10-year overall survival 38% vs 25% with surgery alone, HR 0.70; SCC subgroup median survival 81.6 vs 21.1 months (HR 0.48); NEOCRTEC5010 (SCC, n=451) 5-year 59.9% vs 49.1%; neither trial had a no-surgery arm. Road 2, definitive chemoradiotherapy with salvage (JCOG0909, Japan, cStage II/III SCC, n=94, single arm): 50.4 Gy (1.8 Gy ×28) plus cisplatin/5-FU → complete response 59% → salvage ESD 5% and salvage surgery 27% for residual or recurrent disease (R0 76%, grade 3–4 early complications 20%, 1 operative death) → 5-year overall survival 64.5%, oesophagus preserved at 5 years 54.9%, 3-year overall survival 74.2%. Road 3, active surveillance, marked 'still in trials' (SANO, 12 Dutch hospitals, n=309 with cCR, about three-quarters adenocarcinoma and one-fifth SCC, median follow-up 38 months): chemoradiotherapy → bite-on-bite biopsies at 4–6 weeks → PET-CT plus biopsies plus EUS-FNA at 12 weeks, cCR 37% (274/750) → surveillance with local regrowth in 48% leading to delayed surgery and distant metastasis in 17% → only 25% still in cCR at 54 months; 2-year overall survival 74% vs 71%, non-inferiority met (margin 15%), median 43 vs 53 months (HR 1.14, not significant), distant metastasis trending towards the surgery arm. Three warnings underneath: in preSANO standard biopsies missed 31% and bite-on-bite plus FNA still missed 10%, the SCC preSINO negative predictive value was 68.7%, and only 35.6% of SANO surgery-arm cCR patients were pT0; NEEDS (SCC, about 1,020 patients) is recruiting with primary completion estimated December 2026 and ESOSTRATE was terminated (188 patients); in the other direction, Cochrane found adding surgery gave overall survival HR 0.99 with treatment-related death RR 5.11, and 90-day mortality is 4.5% after planned oesophagectomy and 9.5% after salvage. The three cohorts differ; read each row's numbers only within that row.

g.text: THREE ROADS AFTER CHEMORADIOTHERAPY
Three roads after
chemoradiotherapy: trimodality,
definitive CRT with salvage,
active surveillance
Each road has its own trial, cohort and follow-up; the numbers do not
compare across rows. The third road exists so far only inside trial designs.
The reasons this department still recommends surgery after
chemoradiotherapy for SCC are written under the third road.
Road 1 | Trimodality: chemoradiotherapy, then surgery
The road this department recommends — the one CROSS
and NEOCRTEC5010 proved better than surgery alone
CROSS: the Netherlands, n=366, 75% adenocarcinoma / 23% SCC, cT1N1 /
T2–3N0–1; neither trial had a 'no surgery' arm.
Chemoradiotherapy, 5 weeks
41.4 Gy in 23 fractions + weekly carboplatin/paclitaxel ×5
Surgery
6–8 weeks after chemoradiotherapy; in-hospital mortality 4% in both arms; R0
Pathology report
pCR 29% (SCC 49%, adenocarcinoma 23%); residual tumour → the postoperative
nivolumab box
Long-term follow-up
median follow-up 147 months (Eyck 2021)
10-year OS 38%
vs 25% with surgery alone, HR 0.70; SCC subgroup median OS 81.6 vs 21.1
months (HR 0.48). NEOCRTEC5010 (SCC, n=451): 5-year OS 59.9% vs 49.1%.
Road 2 | Definitive chemoradiotherapy + salvage
Not operating is not giving up: a prospective trial wrote
salvage into the protocol
JCOG0909: Japan, cStage II/III SCC, n=94, single-arm confirmatory trial, no
control arm; ESMO 2025: preferred for patients unwilling or unfit for surgery
and for cervical tumours.
Chemoradiotherapy 50.4 Gy
1.8 Gy ×28 + cisplatin/5-FU; Japan moved from 60 Gy back to 50.4 to reduce
toxicity and salvage-surgery risk
Assess response
complete response 59%; good responders receive 1–2 more chemotherapy cycles
Residual or recurrent → salvage
salvage ESD 5%, salvage surgery 27% (R0 76%; grade 3–4 early complications
20%; 1 operative death)
Follow-up
late grade 3 toxicity 9.6%
5-year OS 64.5%
Oesophagus preserved at 5 years in 54.9% (95% CI 44.3–64.4); 3-year OS
74.2%. Single arm — not directly comparable with road 1.
Road 3 | Active surveillance — still in trials
SANO read out 'non-inferior at two years' — but the
cohort is Dutch adenocarcinoma, follow-up is just over
three years, distant metastasis trends the wrong way and
long-term results are not out yet
SANO: 12 Dutch hospitals, stepped-wedge cluster-randomised, n=309 with cCR
(198 surveillance / 111 surgery), about three-quarters adenocarcinoma and
one-fifth SCC, median follow-up 38 months. No guideline lists it as a standard
option.
Chemoradiotherapy (CROSS regimen)
750 patients treated
Assessment 1: 4–6 weeks
endoscopy with bite-on-bite biopsies
Assessment 2: 12 weeks
PET-CT + biopsies + EUS-FNA → cCR 37% (274/750)
Active surveillance
repeat assessment at 6, 9, 12, 16, 20, 24, 30, 36, 48, 60 months; local regrowth
48% → delayed surgery; distant metastasis 17%
Long term?
only 25% still in cCR at 54 months; the authors concede this may show in OS later
2-year OS 74% vs 71%
Non-inferiority met (margin 15%); median OS 43 vs 53 months (HR 1.14, not
significant); distant metastasis trends towards standard surgery. Better
dysphagia and quality of life at 6 months.
'Not seen' is not 'not there': in preSANO standard biopsies missed 31% of
TRG3–4 residual disease and bite-on-bite + FNA still missed 10%; the SCC
preSINO negative predictive value was 68.7%; of 101 SANO surgery-arm
patients judged cCR, only 36 (35.6%) were pT0 (critics, citing the appendix).
Still being tested: NEEDS (SCC only, ~1,020 patients) is recruiting, primary
completion estimated December 2026; ESOSTRATE (France) was
terminated for slow accrual (188 patients); SANO-2 is checking whether it
can be reproduced outside a trial.
And the other direction: for SCC that responded to chemoradiotherapy,
adding surgery did not improve overall survival (Cochrane HR 0.99) but
raised treatment-related death (RR 5.11); 90-day mortality after planned
oesophagectomy 4.5% (Esodata), after salvage 9.5% (Markar 2014).
The three cohorts differ: road 1 is 75% adenocarcinoma, road 2 all SCC, road 3
three-quarters adenocarcinoma; stages, eras and follow-up differ too — read each
row's numbers only within that row.
Schematic, redrawn from CROSS (van Hagen 2012, Shapiro 2015, Eyck 2021),
NEOCRTEC5010 (Yang 2021), JCOG0909 (Takeuchi 2021; final analysis as cited by JES
2022), SANO (Noordman 2018 design, van der Wilk 2025, Gangaram Panday 2026, Housman
2025 commentary), preSANO (Noordman 2018), preSINO (Yang 2025), Cochrane 2017,
Esodata (Kuppusamy 2022), Markar 2014 and the ClinicalTrials.gov NEEDS/ESOSTRATE
records | cohorts, designs and endpoints differ — numbers are not directly comparable
